# Catto Learning Canonical HTML Course Template

**Generated by:** ChatGPT  
**Date time:** 2026/08/11 15:02 SAST  
**Version:** 2.3  
**Purpose:** Authoring standard for all new self-contained Catto Learning HTML courses intended for clean import into the Catto Learning LMS.  
**Status:** This document supersedes the earlier `Catto Learning Course Template` and `CATTO_LEARNING_HTML_COURSE_AUTHORING_STANDARD.md`.

---

## 1. Core principle

Build every new course to **one fixed structure**. Do not invent alternate markup that happens to look equivalent in a browser.

The Catto Learning importer extracts static HTML and assessment data. It **does not execute the course JavaScript** during import.

The importer does now import the course's `<style>` blocks as scoped course presentation CSS. JavaScript remains relevant to the standalone HTML course, but is not the source of LMS course content.

Therefore:

- content that must survive import must exist as real HTML in the source;
- quiz/question data must exist in the `QUIZ` data object;
- do not rely on JavaScript to generate teaching content;
- use the exact section identities defined below;
- do not put important teaching content inside `.subs`, because `.subs` is removed from the main imported module content after the module summary is extracted.

---

## 2. Canonical section types

Use these exact forms for new courses.

| Type | Canonical opening tag | Question bank |
|---|---|---|
| Standard module with assessment | `<section class="module acc-item" id="mod-m1" data-assessment-required="true">` | `QUIZ.m1` |
| Standard module without assessment | `<section class="module acc-item" id="mod-m2" data-assessment-required="false">` | none |
| Review module with assessment | `<section class="review acc-item" id="mod-review" data-assessment-required="true">` | `QUIZ.review` |
| Review module without assessment | `<section class="review acc-item" id="mod-review" data-assessment-required="false">` | none |
| Final assessment | `<section class="final acc-item" id="final">` | `QUIZ.final` |
| Diagnostic assessment | `<section class="diag acc-item" id="diagnostic">` | `QUIZ.diag` |

### Why `final` and `diagnostic` do not start with `mod-`

The importer identifies normal teaching modules as `<section>` elements whose class contains `module` and whose id begins `mod-`.

Using `id="final"` and `id="diagnostic"` provides an extra safety barrier: even if someone accidentally adds the `module` class later, these course-level assessments cannot be mistaken for ordinary teaching modules.

The dedicated review module is the exception: the importer explicitly recognises `id="mod-review"` and excludes it from the normal-module query.

---

## 3. Document skeleton

Use this overall document structure:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en-ZA">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Course Title</title>

<!-- Optional approved Google Fonts stylesheet links -->
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&amp;display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

<style>
/* All course-specific CSS belongs here. */
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="wrap">

  <header class="masthead" data-level="Intermediate">
    <h1>Course Title</h1>
    <p class="course-subtitle">Course Subtitle</p>
    <p class="course-summary">One-paragraph course summary.</p>
  </header>

  <!-- Optional diagnostic -->

  <div class="modules">
    <!-- Standard teaching modules m1...mN -->
  </div>

  <!-- Optional review module -->

  <!-- Final assessment -->

  <footer>...</footer>
</div>

<script>
const QUIZ = { /* all assessment banks */ };
const REVIEW = { /* optional review-card data */ };
</script>

<script>
/* Standalone-course interaction code may follow. */
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

---

## 4. Course title, subtitle, summary and level

The importer reads four separate course-level metadata fields:

```text
.masthead @data-level      -> course level
.masthead h1               -> course title
.masthead .course-subtitle -> course subtitle
.masthead .course-summary  -> course summary
```

Use this exact structure for every new course:

```html
<header class="masthead" data-level="Beginner">
  <h1>Accounts Payable Essentials</h1>
  <p class="course-subtitle">Professional Short Course</p>
  <p class="course-summary">A practical introduction to the complete accounts payable cycle.</p>
</header>
```

The subtitle and summary are separate concepts. Do not place the subtitle in the `h1`, and do not use an unclassified masthead paragraph for either field in newly authored courses.

### Course level

Every newly authored course must set its level explicitly on the masthead with `data-level`.

```html
<header class="masthead" data-level="Advanced">
```

Normal values are `Beginner`, `Intermediate` and `Advanced`. If a course genuinely uses another level label, place the exact desired label in `data-level`.

The importer **must not infer course level from arbitrary course prose**. Course content often mentions beginner, intermediate or advanced material and those words do not define the course itself. If `data-level` is absent, the importer may inspect the masthead `.eyebrow` as a compatibility fallback only. It never scans the teaching content for level words.

### Title rules

Do not place `<br>` inside the course title.

Do not use a spaced hyphen or em dash as a subtitle inside the `h1`, because the current importer deliberately truncates the title at the first ` - ` or ` — ` style suffix.

Bad:

```html
<h1>Accounts Payable — Professional Short Course</h1>
```

Good:

```html
<h1>Accounts Payable</h1>
<p class="course-subtitle">Professional Short Course</p>
<p class="course-summary">A practical course covering the complete accounts payable process.</p>
```

---

## 5. Standard teaching module WITH assessment

Use this structure consistently.

```html
<section class="module acc-item" id="mod-m1" data-assessment-required="true">
  <button class="acc-trigger module-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="node">
      <span class="num">01</span>
      <span class="check">&#10003;</span>
    </span>

    <span class="m-titles">
      <span class="eyebrow">Module 01</span>
      <span class="m-name">Module Title</span>
      <small>Module subtitle</small>
    </span>

    <span class="m-grade" data-grade></span>
    <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
  </button>

  <div class="acc-panel">
    <div class="acc-inner">
      <div class="module-inner">
        <div class="module-body">

          <div class="outcomes">
            <span class="eyebrow">Learning outcomes</span>
            <ol>
              <li>First learning outcome.</li>
              <li>Second learning outcome.</li>
            </ol>
          </div>

          <!-- Static module teaching content -->
          <h4>Topic heading</h4>
          <p>Teaching content...</p>

          <!-- Optional static collapsible content that must survive import -->
          <div class="blocks">
            <details class="block">
              <summary class="block-head">Worked example</summary>
              <div class="block-inner">
                <p>Static worked-example content...</p>
              </div>
            </details>
          </div>

          <!-- Importer-owned summary/standalone assessment region -->
          <div class="subs">
            <section class="sub s-summary acc-item">
              <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span class="sub-label">Summary</span>
                <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
              </button>
              <div class="acc-panel">
                <div class="acc-inner">
                  <div class="sub-inner">
                    <ul>
                      <li>Summary point one.</li>
                      <li>Summary point two.</li>
                    </ul>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            </section>

            <section class="sub s-assess acc-item">
              <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span class="sub-label">Self Assessment</span>
                <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
              </button>
              <div class="acc-panel">
                <div class="acc-inner">
                  <div class="sub-inner">
                    <div class="quiz" data-quiz="m1"></div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            </section>
          </div>

        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

The corresponding question bank is `QUIZ.m1`.

### Required importer identities

For every normal module:

- element must be `<section>`;
- class must contain the bare word `module`;
- id must be `mod-<module-key>`;
- use canonical sequential keys `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, ...;
- module title must be `.m-name`;
- subtitle should be `.m-titles small`;
- teaching content must be inside `.module-body`;
- learning outcomes must be inside `.outcomes`;
- assessment requirement must be explicitly declared.

---

## 6. Standard teaching module WITHOUT assessment

Use the same module structure, but set:

```html
<section class="module acc-item" id="mod-m2" data-assessment-required="false">
```

Do **not** create `QUIZ.m2`.

Do **not** include an `.s-assess` block or `data-quiz="m2"` placeholder.

The module may still contain:

- learning outcomes;
- full teaching content;
- worked examples;
- practical exercises;
- a module summary.

It simply has no required graded module assessment.

---

## 7. Learning outcomes

Use actual HTML:

```html
<div class="outcomes">
  <span class="eyebrow">Learning outcomes</span>
  <ol>
    <li>Outcome one.</li>
    <li>Outcome two.</li>
  </ol>
</div>
```

The LMS extracts the outcomes and supplies its own Learning Outcomes heading. The importer removes one HTML label whose text is `Learning outcomes` or `Learning outcome` from the stored outcomes content.

### Do not generate the heading with CSS

Do **not** do this:

```css
.outcomes::before {
  content: "Learning outcomes";
}
```

Course CSS is now imported into the LMS. A CSS-generated label can therefore survive and create the duplicated-heading problem we previously encountered.

Use the real HTML label shown above instead.

---

## 8. Module summary and `.subs`

The importer specifically extracts:

```text
.s-summary .sub-inner
```

and turns it into a separate LMS **Module summary** accordion.

After extracting the summary, the importer removes the entire `.subs` container from the main module content.

Therefore:

- `.subs` should contain only standalone-course controls such as `.s-summary` and `.s-assess`;
- never put teaching content inside `.subs`;
- never put a worked example, case study, table, checklist or substantive explanation inside `.subs` if it must appear in the LMS lesson;
- put survivable static collapsible content in `<details>` blocks outside `.subs`.

Recommended:

```html
<div class="blocks">
  <details class="block">
    <summary>Case study</summary>
    <div class="block-inner">
      <p>This content survives import.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>
```

`<details>` and `<summary>` are supported by the LMS HTML sanitizer.

---

## 9. Review module WITH assessment

Catto Learning currently has one canonical review module.

Use:

```html
<section class="review acc-item" id="mod-review" data-assessment-required="true">
  <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="node">R</span>
    <span class="m-titles">
      <span class="eyebrow">Revision</span>
      <span class="m-name">Course Review</span>
      <small>Revision and consolidation</small>
    </span>
    <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
  </button>

  <div class="acc-panel">
    <div class="acc-inner">
      <div class="review-inner">
        <p>Static review material...</p>

        <div id="reviewCards"></div>

        <div class="quiz" data-quiz="review"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

Question bank:

```text
QUIZ.review
```

The importer:

1. imports the static HTML inside `.review-inner`;
2. removes an empty `<div id="reviewCards"></div>` placeholder;
3. appends review cards generated from the `REVIEW` data object;
4. imports `QUIZ.review` if present;
5. treats the assessment as required because `data-assessment-required="true"`.

Do not add the `module` class to the review section.

---

## 10. Review module WITHOUT assessment

Use:

```html
<section class="review acc-item" id="mod-review" data-assessment-required="false">
  <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="m-titles">
      <span class="m-name">Course Review</span>
      <small>Revision and consolidation</small>
    </span>
  </button>

  <div class="acc-panel">
    <div class="acc-inner">
      <div class="review-inner">
        <p>Static review material...</p>
        <div id="reviewCards"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

Do not create `QUIZ.review`.

Still declare:

```javascript
const REVIEW = {};
```

if no structured review cards are required. This avoids an unnecessary importer warning.

### Review ordering

The current importer appends the review module after all normal modules regardless of where `mod-review` appears in the source document.

Therefore always author the review **after the final teaching module**.

---

## 11. Final assessment

The final assessment is a course-level assessment, not a teaching module.

Canonical structure:

```html
<section class="final acc-item" id="final">
  <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="node">&#9733;</span>
    <span class="m-titles">
      <span class="eyebrow">Assessment</span>
      <span class="m-name">Final Assessment</span>
      <small>Integrated course assessment</small>
    </span>
    <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
  </button>

  <div class="acc-panel">
    <div class="acc-inner">
      <div class="final-inner">
        <div class="quiz" data-quiz="final"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

Question bank:

```text
QUIZ.final
```

### Rules

- do not give the section the class `module`;
- do not use an id beginning `mod-` for the canonical final section;
- do not put essential teaching content in this section;
- any instructions needed only by the standalone course may appear here, but the LMS final assessment is built from `QUIZ.final`, not from final-section prose.

---

## 12. Diagnostic assessment

A diagnostic is a course-level, non-graded assessment used to tell a learner what they already know and which modules need revision.

Canonical structure:

```html
<section class="diag acc-item" id="diagnostic">
  <button class="acc-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="node">D</span>
    <span class="m-titles">
      <span class="eyebrow">Diagnostic</span>
      <span class="m-name">Course Diagnostic</span>
      <small>Check your existing knowledge before starting</small>
    </span>
    <span class="chev">&#8250;</span>
  </button>

  <div class="acc-panel">
    <div class="acc-inner">
      <div class="diag-inner">
        <p>This diagnostic does not contribute to the course grade.</p>
        <div class="quiz" data-quiz="diag"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

Question bank:

```text
QUIZ.diag
```

Optional pass percentage:

```javascript
const DIAG_PASS = 70;
```

If omitted, the importer defaults the diagnostic pass mark to 50%.

The diagnostic:

- does not contribute to the course grade;
- is not a teaching module;
- may recommend modules for revision;
- may have a pass threshold;
- imports as a real LMS diagnostic assessment.

The importer also recognises legacy diagnostic bank names `diagnostic`, `prereq`, `prerequisite` and `readiness`, but **new courses must use `diag`**.

---

## 13. Diagnostic remediation mappings

A diagnostic question may identify the modules that should be recommended when the learner answers incorrectly.

Use `u`:

```javascript
{
  "q": "Which document authorises payment to a supplier?",
  "o": [
    "Purchase order",
    "Bank statement",
    "Payslip",
    "Delivery route"
  ],
  "a": 0,
  "p": 1,
  "e": "The purchase order is part of the procurement and authorisation trail.",
  "u": ["m2", "m3"]
}
```

Use module keys such as `m2`, not full element ids such as `mod-m2`.

**Remediation references must always be explicit module-key strings. Numeric shortcuts are invalid.**

Correct:

```javascript
"u": ["m3", "m6"]
```

Incorrect:

```javascript
"u": [3, 6]
```

The LMS importer does not infer a prefix from numbers. Numeric remediation references are ignored and generate an import warning.

---

## 14. `QUIZ` assessment data

Put all question banks in one declaration.

For new courses, use strict JSON-style JavaScript:

```javascript
const QUIZ = {
  "m1": [
    {
      "q": "Question text?",
      "o": ["Option A", "Option B", "Option C", "Option D"],
      "a": 1,
      "p": 1,
      "e": "Explanation of the correct answer."
    }
  ],

  "review": [
    {
      "q": "Review question?",
      "o": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
      "a": 2,
      "p": 2,
      "e": "Explanation."
    }
  ],

  "diag": [
    {
      "q": "Diagnostic question?",
      "o": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
      "a": 0,
      "p": 1,
      "e": "Explanation.",
      "u": ["m1", "m4"]
    }
  ],

  "final": [
    {
      "q": "Integrated final question?",
      "o": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
      "a": 3,
      "p": 3,
      "e": "Explanation."
    }
  ]
};
```

### Canonical question fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `q` | yes | Question stem |
| `o` | yes | Answer options |
| `a` | yes | Zero-based correct-option index |
| `p` | no | Points; also maps to difficulty (`1` introductory, `2` standard, `3+` advanced) |
| `e` | no | Explanation |
| `u` | diagnostic only | Module keys recommended after an incorrect diagnostic answer |

`a` is zero-based:

```text
0 = first option
1 = second option
2 = third option
3 = fourth option
```

### Option count

For consistency, new multiple-choice questions should normally use **four options**.

The importer can accept other option counts as long as the correct index is valid, so genuine true/false or other deliberate formats are permitted. Do not vary option counts casually.

### Invalid questions

A question without `q`, `o` or `a`, with no options, or with an invalid answer index is skipped by the importer. Therefore validate every bank before delivery.

---

## 15. `REVIEW` data

Structured review cards use:

```javascript
const REVIEW = {
  "m1": {
    "t": "Module 1 key points",
    "pts": [
      "First review point.",
      "Second review point."
    ]
  }
};
```

If a review module exists but no structured cards are needed, use:

```javascript
const REVIEW = {};
```

Do not rely on JavaScript to populate other substantive review content. Static review prose must already exist inside `.review-inner`.

---

## 16. Static HTML versus JavaScript-generated content

The importer does not run the standalone course JavaScript.

Therefore this is unsafe for content that must import:

```html
<div id="workedExample"></div>
<script>
workedExample.innerHTML = "Important teaching material";
</script>
```

The importer sees an empty `<div>`.

Instead write:

```html
<div id="workedExample">
  <p>Important teaching material.</p>
</div>
```

JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but it must not be the sole source of important teaching content.

The special `reviewCards` placeholder is an exception because the LMS knows how to rebuild it from the `REVIEW` object.

---

## 17. CSS and interactive sub-content

Course `<style>` blocks are imported and scoped beneath the LMS course-presentation wrapper. Approved Google Fonts stylesheet links are also preserved.

That means source CSS can affect imported course content, so CSS must be written deliberately.

For collapsible teaching material **inside** a module, prefer native HTML:

```html
<details>
  <summary>Worked example</summary>
  <p>Content...</p>
</details>
```

rather than building another JavaScript-only accordion.

This gives the standalone file usable interaction while leaving meaningful static HTML for the importer.

---

## 18. Markup and escaping

- Use unique HTML `id` values throughout the document.
- Entity-encode `&`, `<` and `>` when they are literal data in HTML text or attributes.
- Inside JavaScript strings, be particularly careful never to include a literal `</script>` sequence; write `<\/script>` if such text is genuinely required.
- Other ordinary closing tags such as `</b>` do **not** need to be escaped merely because they appear in a JavaScript string.
- Keep JavaScript data declarations syntactically valid.
- Do not use comments or trailing commas inside the canonical `QUIZ` and `REVIEW` data declarations.

---

## 19. Recommended course order

Use this order:

```text
Masthead / course introduction
Diagnostic assessment (optional)
Module 1
Module 2
Module 3
...
Final teaching module
Review module (optional)
Final assessment
Footer
QUIZ / REVIEW data
Standalone course JavaScript
```

---

## 20. Conformance checklist

Before delivering any new course HTML, verify **every module**, not just the first one.

### Course-level

- [ ] `.masthead` has an explicit `data-level` value.
- [ ] One `.masthead h1` contains the clean course title.
- [ ] `.masthead .course-subtitle` contains the course subtitle.
- [ ] `.masthead .course-summary` contains the course summary.
- [ ] Course title contains no `<br>` and no spaced dash suffix intended as a subtitle.
- [ ] All teaching module keys are sequential: `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, ...
- [ ] One `const QUIZ = {...};` declaration contains all assessment banks.
- [ ] `const REVIEW = {...};` exists if a review module exists.
- [ ] Diagnostic, if present, uses `class="diag"`, `id="diagnostic"`, `data-quiz="diag"` and `QUIZ.diag`.
- [ ] Final uses `class="final"`, `id="final"`, `data-quiz="final"` and `QUIZ.final`.
- [ ] Final and diagnostic do not have class `module` and do not use ids beginning `mod-`.
- [ ] Review, if present, is exactly `id="mod-review"` and has `.review-inner`.
- [ ] No duplicate element ids.

### Every standard teaching module

- [ ] Element is `<section>`.
- [ ] Class contains `module`.
- [ ] Id is `mod-mN`.
- [ ] Explicit `data-assessment-required="true"` or `"false"`.
- [ ] `.m-name` exists.
- [ ] `.m-titles small` contains the subtitle.
- [ ] `.module-body` exists.
- [ ] `.outcomes` exists and contains actual outcomes.
- [ ] The words `Learning outcomes` are not generated using CSS pseudo-elements.
- [ ] Important teaching content exists statically in `.module-body`.
- [ ] `.s-summary .sub-inner` exists when a module summary is required.
- [ ] No substantive teaching content is trapped inside `.subs`.
- [ ] If assessment required: matching `QUIZ.mN` exists and is non-empty.
- [ ] If assessment not required: no orphan `QUIZ.mN` bank is generated.

### Every question

- [ ] `q`, `o`, `a` exist.
- [ ] `o` contains sensible unique options.
- [ ] `a` points to an existing option.
- [ ] `p` is a positive integer when supplied.
- [ ] `e` explains the correct answer where useful.
- [ ] Diagnostic `u` mappings refer to valid module keys.

---

## 21. Validation sequence

Before delivery:

1. Run JavaScript syntax validation (`node --check` on the script content or equivalent).
2. Confirm `QUIZ` and `REVIEW` are valid JSON-style object literals.
3. Reconcile every `mod-mN` section against its assessment requirement and `QUIZ.mN` bank.
4. Check every question's correct-answer index.
5. Check duplicate HTML ids.
6. Check the source HTML with an HTML parser and review real structural warnings.
7. Run the Catto Learning importer itself.
8. Confirm in the import preview:
   - course title and summary;
   - module count and ordering;
   - subtitles;
   - learning outcomes;
   - module summaries;
   - assessment-required flags;
   - module question counts;
   - review module and review assessment if used;
   - diagnostic and its remediation mappings if used;
   - final assessment and question count;
   - presentation CSS detection.

**The importer preview is the final authority.** A source file that looks correct in a browser but imports incorrectly is not conformant.

---

## 22. Instruction to the course-generating AI

When generating a Catto Learning course:

1. Follow this document literally.
2. Do not invent alternative section ids, module keys, assessment bank names or equivalent structures.
3. Use `m1`, `m2`, `m3`, ... sequentially.
4. Explicitly decide for each module whether an assessment is required.
5. Keep important teaching content as static HTML.
6. Use `details/summary` for collapsible teaching material that must survive import.
7. Use `.subs` only for the module summary and standalone assessment interface.
8. Use real HTML for the Learning Outcomes label; never CSS-generated label text.
9. Use one strict JSON-style `QUIZ` object.
10. Validate the completed file against the checklist before delivery.
11. Do not modify the canonical structure merely for stylistic preference. Styling may vary; importer identities may not.
